tasks.source: the Port of Barcelona's 2024 container calls at quays 24B (APM Terminals Barcelona) and 36A (Terminal Catalunya, BEST), as PortSimEnv's dock-v1-eval one-week standard and busy weeks, with the port's 2024 pilot and tug traffic; the wind that blew at Meteocat's XEMA station Y7 and the ECMWF open-data forecasts as issued, in real Barcelona weather weeks of 2023 to 2025
tasks.selection: 15 marine weeks moved into real weather weeks, dealt from the 240 pairs of the 15 marine weeks and 16 weather weeks where (a) the forecast-following re-planner costs no more than hindsight in at least 3 of its 4 configurations, (b) the re-planner blind to the wind (in a week whose forecast warned of a gale that never came, the one holding every warned window) scores at most 0.9 in at least 3 of 4, (c) the week has at most 10 watches and (d) no ship alongside at hour 0 is due to leave inside a window above 30 kn

grading.reference: min(the hindsight optimum, the best cost of the forecast-following re-planner over its 4 solver configurations)
grading.reward: a feasible week scores 0.2 + 0.8 exp(-g/0.5), g = max(0, cost - reference) / (max(0, reference - floor) + 100), the floor being the cost no plan can avoid; a week that breaks a rule scores 0.2 times its share of clean ships, below 0.2, and a ship left without a window breaks a rule; graded once, on the windows confirmed and the week as it really happened
grading.excused: cost or rule breaks that news, or wind the forecast didn't show at that ship's last chance, brings to a window after its last chance to change, per ship; wind the forecast showed then is charged
